payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Afton, Clarissa, Elda, Jessenia, Lenna, Sheri

payload.content: Planning: Lenna (mobile-dev skill, 7h avail). I’m considering taking ISSUE-0001::triage (effort 1.6, cost 1.46, medium) or maybe ISSUE-0001::docs/review/test. Will avoid ISSUE-0002 tasks (effort/cost high vs availability). What are you taking so we don’t duplicate?
Request: please reply with your candidate task choices for conflict-free planning. I will likely claim ISSUE-0001::triage if unclaimed.

Planning (iter=1): Clarissa here. With 7h mobile-dev skill, my best fit cost-wise is ISSUE-0001::triage (effort 1.6, priority medium, cost 1.71). To avoid duplicates, I’m okay if Lenna takes triage; otherwise I propose taking ISSUE-0001::docs or review next (both medium, costs 2.13). Please confirm what you’re taking so we don’t collide.

Clarissa candidate: ISSUE-0001::triage (effort 1.6, medium). If Lenna wants it, I’ll take ISSUE-0001::docs (effort 2.0, medium) or ISSUE-0001::review (effort 2.0 review, medium) depending on what’s left.

Planning update (Jessenia): my best feasible/low-cost options are ISSUE-0001::triage (effort 1.6, cost 1.65) or ISSUE-0001::review (effort 2.0, cost 2.06) or ISSUE-0001::docs/test (higher cost). To avoid duplicates: I can take ISSUE-0001::review if triage is taken by Lenna/Clarissa; otherwise I’m willing to take ISSUE-0001::triage.

Planning update (Elda): I’m mobile-development strong (0.95) and 8h avail. My top cost-effective choices are ISSUE-0001::triage (effort 1.6, cost 1.53, medium) or ISSUE-0001::review (effort 2.0, cost 1.91, medium). To avoid duplicates: if triage is already taken, I can take ISSUE-0001::review or ISSUE-0001::docs (cost 1.91). I will not take ISSUE-0002 tasks unless everything else is taken.
Sheri here: to avoid duplicates with triage, I'm leaning to ISSUE-0001::review or ISSUE-0001::docs if triage is taken. Will skip ISSUE-0002.

Afton (phase=planning): For conflict-free planning, my best feasible choice is ISSUE-0001::implement (effort 4.0, medium). I will avoid ISSUE-0002 due to high effort/cost. If someone else takes implement, I can take ISSUE-0001::triage (effort 1.6) as backup to keep tasks from being left unclaimed. Please confirm your intended claim.

Lenna planning response: I will claim ISSUE-0001::triage (effort 1.6, medium). Will not take other ISSUE-0001 tasks to avoid duplicates. Please coordinate remaining work (docs/review/test/implement) among the others.

Clarissa planning confirm: Lenna claimed ISSUE-0001::triage. I will avoid duplicate triage. Next-best feasible/low-cost medium tasks for me are ISSUE-0001::docs (effort 2.0, cost 2.13) or ISSUE-0001::review (effort 2.0, cost 2.13). Please tell others if you plan to take docs vs review vs test; I’m aiming for conflict-free choice.

Clarissa suggestion: keep medium-priority coverage by assigning one of docs/review/test to someone and implement to Afton (already considering). I can take ISSUE-0001::docs or ISSUE-0001::review depending on who hasn’t claimed.

Planning (Jessenia): I see Lenna will take ISSUE-0001::triage. To avoid duplicates, I will aim for ISSUE-0001::review (effort 2.0, medium) in execution. If review is taken by another, I will switch to ISSUE-0001::docs; otherwise skip.
Elda planning (iter=1): Lenna already claimed ISSUE-0001::triage. I will take ISSUE-0001::review (effort 2.0, medium) if unclaimed; otherwise I can take ISSUE-0001::docs. Will avoid ISSUE-0002 tasks.
Planning update: Lenna confirms claim on ISSUE-0001::triage. Will not take any other task to avoid duplicates; happy to rely on others for docs/review/test/implement.

Clarissa planning (iter=1): Lenna already takes ISSUE-0001::triage. I will avoid duplicates and next claim either ISSUE-0001::docs or ISSUE-0001::review. If either is already taken in execution plan, I will take skip rather than risk collision; otherwise my top choice is ISSUE-0001::docs (effort 2.0, medium, cost 2.13) due to lower effort than review/test.

Jessenia planning: I will target ISSUE-0001::review in execution (effort 2.0, medium, cost 2.06) since triage is taken by Lenna. If review ends up claimed by someone else, I can switch to ISSUE-0001::docs; otherwise skip to avoid duplicates. Let me know your intended final claim for review/docs.
Planning update (Elda): Lenna has ISSUE-0001::triage. I will claim ISSUE-0001::review (effort 2.0, medium) in execution to avoid duplicates; will not take ISSUE-0002.

Lenna (planning, iter1): I will take ISSUE-0001::triage (effort 1.6, medium). To avoid collisions, I will not claim docs/review/test/implement. Please coordinate among you for remaining medium tasks (docs/review) and leave implement to Afton if chosen.

Planning update (iter=1): Clarissa confirms I will aim to claim ISSUE-0001::docs (effort 2.0, medium) in execution to avoid duplicating Elda/Jessenia on review and Lenna on triage. If docs is taken, I will skip rather than risk duplicate. (phase=planning)

Jessenia planning sync: Lenna has ISSUE-0001::triage. I intend to claim ISSUE-0001::review in execution (effort 2.0, medium, cost 2.06). If Elda/others also take review, my fallback is ISSUE-0001::docs; otherwise I will skip to avoid duplicates. Please confirm you won’t also claim review/docs.

Elda planning: confirmed—Lenna has triage; I intend to claim ISSUE-0001::review (effort 2.0, medium) in execution. I will not take docs/test/implement or any ISSUE-0002 tasks to avoid duplicate claims.
Afton planning (confirm): I intend ISSUE-0001::implement (medium, effort 4.0) and will not claim triage/review/docs/test to avoid duplicates. Sheri on ISSUE-0001::review per coalition.
